newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rights body says five died in riots.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rights body says five died in riots.

text.p: Indonesia's official human rights commission said on Saturday five people had died, 149 were injured and 23 were still missing as a result of July 27 riots that rocked the capital Jakarta.
The National Commission on Human Rights released the figures in its final official report on the disturbances, the worst in the Indonesian capital in more than two decades.
The commission said in an earlier preliminary report that five people had died, 149 people were injured and 74 were missing. The government called on the commission to justify the figures.
The secretary-general of the commission, Bachruddin Lopa, said while releasing the report that "the authorities must continue to look for those who are missing".

The riots were sparked by a police assault on the Jakarta headquarters of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party to evict followers of Megawati Sukarnoputri, who had been ousted as party leader by a government-backed faction in June.
